source.title: Beyond a Single Direction: Chain-of-Thought Disrupts Simple Steering of Refusal
source.authors: Kia-Jung Yang; Dominik Meier; Jia-Chen Zhao; T. Ruas; B. Gipp

record.file_problem: The paper text is substantially readable and includes appendices; there are minor extraction artifacts, including a clipped opening fragment in the abstract and malformed symbols in examples.
record.tranche_reason: It applies a difference-in-means refusal direction and activation steering, then measures harmful-request compliance in a reasoning model. This is the original-style intervention in a new model setting, although it does not perform the original all-layer projection ablation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports harmful-request compliance rates for steering with fixed, suppressed, regenerated, and swapped CoTs. The reported summary rates are retained; the layer-by-layer values in Figures 1–3 are not stated in the text, and the paper says results vary across layers. Appendix A's refusal-classifier accuracy evaluates the classifier, not the claim's behavior, so it is not a row. The cited results from other work are not rows. Illustrative individual examples in the appendices are not separately quantified results.
record.test_reason: It applies a difference-in-means refusal direction to a reasoning model (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B) and reports harmful-request compliance under fixed, suppressed and regenerated CoT. It argues that a single template-token direction does not fully mediate refusal in LRMs, which bears directly on V8 and on V1 in this setting. It uses activation addition at one layer rather than all-layer ablation, so the evidence is close to, but not the same as, the original recipe.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is largely correct. The authors also state that this joint encoding in activations and CoT makes LRMs more robust to activation-only interventions. They add that the CoT becomes a new attack surface, and suggest detecting the refusal signal and suppressing the CoT as a defense.
record.recipe_differences: Uses difference-in-means activations from harmful and harmless instructions and activation steering, but steers at EOI or EOT template-token positions and selected layers rather than projecting out the direction at every layer and position. It tests a reasoning model and varies whether CoT is fixed, suppressed, regenerated, or swapped.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome varies with CoT handling (fixed, suppressed, regenerated, or swapped) and across steering layers; the text does not provide exact layer-specific rates.

fits_no_version.finding: A CoT generated under steering, reused without any steering, still yields 48% compliance; the original CoT reinforces refusal against steering.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In reasoning models, the generated CoT carries and can reconstruct the refusal or compliance state independently of the residual-stream direction.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306 (2026)
record.problems: Only one model is evaluated, as the authors acknowledge. Layer-dependent results are shown in figures but exact layer-specific rates are not stated in the text. The paper does not test other abilities, harmless-request refusals, or the full all-layer ablation. The authors also state that they did not establish whether the generated CoT is faithful or causally responsible for the final behavior.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 1–3 show compliance across layers, but the text gives no exact layer-specific values; the reported summary rates are recorded in R2–R5. Appendix A's classifier-accuracy results and the appendices' illustrative single examples are omitted because they do not provide separate aggregate tests of the claim.

untested.parts: All-layer, all-position projection ablation; adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts; preservation of other capabilities.
Any reasoning model other than DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B; ablation (as opposed to single-layer addition); capability preservation.
Not tested: no weight edit or abliteration.
Not tested: no comparison of multi-direction, cone or affine geometry.

missing.what: Per-layer compliance curves for each condition. The rows report only maxima, and the optimal layer and steering magnitude α are never stated.

record.verdict_notes: There is a single model and no uncertainty estimates. The refusal measure is inconsistent: the main text cites Arditi et al.'s refusal score, while Appendix A justifies using Llama Guard as the classifier. The steering coefficient α is unspecified. Reported rates appear to be best-layer maxima ('up to'). The V4 link in the record conflates the CoT contribution with multi-direction geometry.

versions.untested_parts: Tests steering along a difference-in-means direction on harmful requests, but not projection-out ablation at every layer and position, steering to induce refusal on harmless requests, or preservation of other abilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration test.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Tests an additional CoT contribution, not affine or cone geometry among residual-stream directions.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test.
Does not compare refusal-training methods, timing, or training stages.
Tests one reasoning model only; does not establish generality across reasoning models or directly test the full all-layer ablation and capability-preservation claim.

relation.reason: Its own steering results with a diff-in-means direction on refusal bear directly on V1 in a reasoning model (V8).

tranche.reason: The method differs from the original: one-layer negative activation addition at EOI/EOT tokens, and a fixed, suppressed or regenerated CoT, rather than ablation at all layers. So T1 (the reader's call) is wrong. The study argues explicitly that a single template-token direction doesn't fully mediate refusal in reasoning models, which fits T5.

source_check.notes: Single model, 100 JailbreakBench prompts, greedy decoding. All values are layer-sweep maxima with alpha and layer unstated. There is no random-direction control and no capability measure. The judge is a Llama Guard model, named inconsistently (Llama-3.2-8B-Guard / Llama-3-8B-Guard); it scored 0.86 accuracy on 50 hand-labelled responses. The 48% CoT-swap result (Sec. 4.4) is not among the rows checked here.

statements.problem: The 39%, 70% and 94% figures are right for DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B with EOI steering. R3 (EOT, 43%) is cited but the statement doesn't mention it.
Minor: 'best layer' for 94% is inferred from the Figure 3 layer sweep. The text says only 'reaching 94% (Figure 3)'.

statements.correction: Sec. 4.1: 39% (EOI) and 43% (EOT) with the CoT fixed, called significantly weaker than LLMs. Sec. 4.2: 70% with the CoT suppressed, still short of typical LLM steering.
statements.problem: Minor: 'significantly weaker than in standard LLMs' is said only of the fixed-CoT 39-43% results (Sec. 4.1). For 70% the authors say it 'still falls short' of LLM steering.

statements.correction: arXiv:2605.26772, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B: negative activation addition along the EOI/EOT diff-in-means direction at one layer. Compliance up to 39% (EOI) and 43% (EOT) with the unsteered CoT held fixed, 70% with the CoT suppressed, 94% with the CoT regenerated under steering, from 0%.
statements.problem: 'At most 39-43% with the CoT kept' is right, but it is set against removal results without saying that the study's own condition with the CoT regenerated under steering reaches 94%. That condition is the one closest to interventions applied during generation, and it agrees with them. Also, the study uses activation addition with a negative coefficient at one layer, not directional ablation.

statements.correction: Add: arXiv:2605.26772, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, CoT fixed: EOI-token direction up to 39%, EOT-token direction up to 43% compliance (best layer, 0% baseline). Or drop the R2/R3 citation.
statements.problem: Cites rows R2 and R3 from this study, but the statement says nothing about it. The study is relevant to the factor (extraction token): EOI vs EOT.
The 39%, 70% and 94% figures with EOI steering match Table 1 and Sec. 4.1-4.3.

reader_labels.label: supports

reader_labels.reason: The high compliance with regenerated CoT and the retained 48% after swapping in a steered CoT support an additional CoT-carried signal alongside residual-stream steering (R5–R6).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: In this reasoning model, steering yields 39–43% compliance with fixed CoT and 70% with CoT suppressed, rather than consistently eliminating refusal (R2–R4).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Steering with a regenerated CoT reaches 94% compliance, while a previously steered CoT without active steering retains 48%, indicating that the effect depends on the CoT condition (R5–R6).
